Look at what happens when weak-kneed politicians try to meddle with basic market realities just to appease the progressive mob. Taoiseach Micheál Martin went down to Limerick this past week bragging that housing tenancies have increased, but the truth on the ground is that families are suffering because the government caved to activist pressure and imposed new rules on March 1 forcing landlords to provide six-year leases for tenants. 

Naturally, property owners pushed back against this heavy-handed state overreach, and now we are seeing a rise in eviction notices and homelessness, with the numbers of people in emergency accommodation nationally increasing again. When the state interferes with private property and contracts, it inevitably undermines social order and stability, punishing the very people it pretends to help. Instead of standing up for traditional stability and personal responsibility, the political establishment just pushes more regulation, creating chaos and throwing families out onto the streets while patting themselves on the back.
